subtopics.title: Label sides of right-angled triangle
subtopics.exposition: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite to the right-angle is labelled the hypotenuse. With respect to an angle θ in a right-angled triangle, the side opposite θ is labelled "opposite". With respect to an angle θ in a right-angled triangle, the side next to θ is labelled "adjacent". The hypotenuse remains the same regardless of which internal angle is being referred to. The hypotenuse is always opposite the right-angle and is always the longest side. The opposite and adjacent sides depend on the angle being looked at. Either non-90° internal angle of a right-angled triangle can be chosen, and the adjacent and opposite sides are then defined accordingly. To label the sides, first find the right angle; the hypotenuse is directly opposite the right angle and is found first because it never changes position. The opposite side relative to the angle θ is the side directly opposite the angle θ. The adjacent side is the remaining side of the triangle (after the hypotenuse and the opposite side) and must be one of the sides that forms the angle θ. For the other angle α, the opposite and adjacent sides switch places compared with θ. In the worked example the hypotenuse is still AC when the angle considered is α instead of θ. In a right-angled triangle the three sides are named according to how they are placed in relation to the angle θ.

subtopics.title: Write sin, cos, tan ratios
subtopics.exposition: sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse. cos θ = adjacent / hypotenuse. tan θ = opposite / adjacent. The ratios of similar triangles are used to define the trigonometric ratios. It does not matter what the lengths of the sides of the triangles are: if the angle remains constant, the ratio of the sides will always yield the same answer. In similar triangles ABC and DEF, ratios between corresponding sides are equal: AB/BC = DE/EF, AB/AC = DE/DF and AC/BC = DF/EF. In similar triangles ABC and DEF, AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF. In similar triangles ABC and DEF, the angle at vertex A equals the angle at vertex D, the angle at vertex B equals the angle at vertex E, and the angle at vertex C equals the angle at vertex F. The trigonometric ratios relate the lengths of the sides of a right-angled triangle to its interior angles. Once the hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent sides are labelled with respect to the angle, complete the trigonometric ratios for that angle from the definitions and name which two sides each ratio uses. In the worked example triangle, for angle θ: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = CB/AC, so sin θ uses sides CB and AC. In the worked example triangle, for angle θ: cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = AB/AC, so cos θ uses sides AB and AC. In the worked example triangle, for angle θ: tan θ = opposite/adjacent = CB/AB, so tan θ uses sides CB and AB. In the worked example triangle, for angle α: sin α = opposite/hypotenuse = AB/AC, so sin α uses sides AB and AC. In the worked example triangle, for angle α: cos α = adjacent/hypotenuse = CB/AC, so cos α uses sides CB and AC. In the worked example triangle, for angle α: tan α = opposite/adjacent = AB/CB, so tan α uses sides AB and CB. That triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF is written △ABC ||| △DEF. The order of letters for similar triangles is very important: similar triangles are always labelled in corresponding order, so △ABC ||| △DEF is correct but △ABC ||| △DFE is incorrect. The three trigonometric ratios of an angle are sine (sin), cosine (cos) and tangent (tan). "Soh Cah Toa" is a mnemonic technique for remembering the trigonometric ratios sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent.

subtopics.title: Write reciprocal ratios
subtopics.exposition: Each of the three trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan) has a reciprocal. cosec θ = 1 / sin θ. sec θ = 1 / cos θ. cot θ = 1 / tan θ. cosec θ = hypotenuse / opposite. sec θ = hypotenuse / adjacent. cot θ = adjacent / opposite. The reciprocal ratios can also be defined for any right-angled triangle in terms of its sides. sin θ × cosec θ = 1. cos θ × sec θ = 1. tan θ × cot θ = 1. The reciprocal ratios are called cosecant (cosec), secant (sec) and cotangent (cot). Cosecant may also be abbreviated as csc.

sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse.

Always check that the triangle has a right-angle before using the trigonometric ratios, otherwise the answer will be wrong.
